title: I spent 3 weeks building a fully destructible voxel game with Claude, then paused the project—releasing the free demo so it doesn't go to waste (CELLBREAKERS)
author: KometUnit1108
selftext:
\*Since I am Japanese, the language in the attached gameplay video is Japanese. Please be aware of this in advance.

Together with Claude, I made a game called “CELLBREAKERS,” **where you rescue friends in a voxel world where you can destroy just about anything.**  
But actually, I gave up on this project about three days ago. So, all that’s left now is the latest version and the demo.  
However, I found a demo page on [Itch.io](http://itch.io/) that I hadn’t published yet. **I’m going to publish it now.** You can download it and play for free, so please give it a try.  
**(There's a link to the page in the comments.)**  


**\[What Makes the Game Fun\]**  
・**Since you can destroy anything, you can play strategically.** (Use stealth, or blow walls up with dynamite.)  
・**The prison is procedurally generated every time, so I think you’ll never get bored.**  
・In addition to procedural generation, there are several environment types (a snow-locked prison, a desert prison, a late-night prison, a sunset prison, etc.).  
・If there’s enough demand, I might even release the full version—which I was actually planning to sell on Steam sometime next year. (It’s not finished yet, but it will include multiplayer and additional environment types.)  


**\[How I Used AI\]**  
・I made this in about three weeks using Opus 5.5. The audio and graphics are generated by code.  
・To avoid it becoming just another “AIslop,” I came up with the ideas myself and used Opus 5.5’s “effort: x-high” setting as a tool to bring them to life.

Finally, there were various reasons why I gave up, but my head just got too cluttered. So, to draw a line under it, I deleted everything—now only the latest version and its demo remain.
